title: Carrington 1859: The Night the Sky Set Telegraph Wires Ablaze
summary: Tells how, on the first of September, eighteen fifty-nine, the English astronomer Richard Carrington saw a white flash of light on the face of the Sun, and how, about seventeen hours later, the largest geomagnetic storm on record struck the Earth, setting telegraph lines ablaze across Europe and North America and carrying the aurora as far as the Caribbean. The episode ranges from the operators who were given electric shocks and the telegraph paper that caught fire, to the Boston–Portland line that kept working with its batteries disconnected, on current drawn from the sky alone, to the gold miners in the Rocky Mountains who rose at midnight thinking it was morning, and on to the question of what the same storm would do to today's world.
